vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The one class of update that stays manual. These bypass the release-age cooldown by design (that is the point of a security alert), and a hijacked package typically ships its payload AS a version that resolves an advisory -- so automerging here would hand same-day, unreviewed CI execution to precisely the most attacker-timed PRs, and this repo's CI holds real secrets (GEMINI_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_LOCAL_TOKEN). The site is static, so a delayed fix carries almost no runtime risk, while a bad automerge carries a real one. They land immediately and are labelled, so they are visible at a glance; merging is a deliberate click.

packageRules.description: Every non-major update, all managers, lands in one PR that merges itself once the CI Gate passes. Nothing here should need a human on a normal month. This also automerges github-actions and pip_requirements, which used to be manual; Python bumps are covered by the Python Script Tests job, but note that job runs pytest and ruff only -- it does not exercise the GitHub/ORCID/AI network paths, which still surface first on the monthly run.

Majors automerge too, but stay in their own PRs so one bad major cannot hold back everything else. The 14-day age is the real safety mechanism: it means this repo is never the first to hit a broken release. Safe only because CI Gate (typecheck, build, unit, e2e, visual regression, Python scripts) is the required status check on main -- automerge waits on required checks only, so if CI Gate is ever dropped from branch protection this silently becomes merge-without-testing. Note the Cloudflare preview job is deliberately NOT required: preview.yml has a paths filter that skips .github/**, and a workflow skipped by a paths filter never reports a status, so requiring it would deadlock every actions-only PR forever. Actions it alone exercises are handled by the last rule instead.

Astro core and integrations must move in lockstep on a major (astro v7 requires @astrojs/mdx v7). Widens the built-in monorepo group to any @astrojs/* package, including ones published outside withastro/astro.
React runtime and its DefinitelyTyped types live in separate repos, so the built-in monorepo group misses @types/react. Keep them in one major PR.

Actions a green CI Gate does not actually exercise, so automerging them would ship them untested and they would first fail at the moment they are needed. Three distinct reasons: (1) create-github-app-token and create-pull-request run only in update-contributions.yml, which triggers on schedule/workflow_dispatch, so no PR ever runs them and a break first appears on the monthly job; (2) wrangler-action and sticky-pull-request-comment run only in preview.yml, whose paths filter skips .github/** -- so a PR bumping just those actions does not trigger the very workflow that would test them, and a break silently kills previews for every later PR; (3) upload-artifact is only reached under `if: failure()`, so a green run never touches it and a break surfaces exactly when a Playwright report is needed to debug something else. Deploy-only actions (deploy-pages, upload-pages-artifact, github-script) are deliberately left automerging: they run on every push to main, so they fail loudly right after merge instead of lying in wait. Given its own group rather than an automerge exception inside the 29-package non-major group, so that group keeps one unambiguous automerge setting.
